title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous pages set up index conventions: upper dots for cochain complexes, lower dots for chain complexes, stars for (co)simplicial objects, and a duality convention. This page states and unpacks a Yoneda/Dold–Kan statement.

Prop. 2. Let Ss be simplicial sets, i.e. presheaves on Δ, written Δ^. Let A and B be additive categories with the needed (co)completeness.
(a) Functors Ss → A commuting with inductive limits correspond to cosimplicial objects of A (their values on the standard simplices Δ^n). By Dold–Kan these are the same as non-negative cochain complexes A^·.
(b) Functors Ss^op → B sending colimits to limits correspond to simplicial objects of B, hence by Dold–Kan to chain complexes B_·.

Unpacking (b) for B = Ab:
- Given K_· = (K_n, d_n), let K_* be the associated simplicial abelian group.
- Set F(X_*) = Hom_{Δ^}(X_*, K_*).
- By the free–forgetful adjunction this equals Hom_{Ab_*}(Z(X_*), K_*), where Z(X_*) = (n ↦ Z^{(X_n)}) is the free simplicial abelian group on X_*, also written C_*(X_*).
- Applying the Dold–Puppe normalization N (written ND), which is an equivalence Ab_* ≃ Ab_·, gives the boxed formula F_{K_·}(X_*) = Hom_{Ab_·}(C_·(X_*), K_·), where C_·(X_*) = N(Z X_*) is the normalized chain complex.

Two conclusions:
1°) Every such 'additive' invariant of X_* factors through the abelianization C_*(X_*), equivalently through C_·(X_*). So C_·(X_*) is 'the universal additive invariant' of X_*. Regarded as functors of C_·, these F are exactly the representable functors on Ab_·.
2°) The NB, continued on the next page: if F carries extra structure, such as a multiplication F⊗F → F making it Z-algebra valued, that structure on F(X_*) cannot be recovered from C_· alone. One must use the extra structure C_· inherits from coming from a simplicial set, i.e. a diagonal/coalgebra structure.

The next page treats k-linear structure, which only requires C_k = C ⊗ k. It also treats a general complete additive B, using an internal Hom(A, M) for A ∈ Ab, M ∈ B and the Z^0 of a Hom bicomplex.

The page serves to motivate the study of cosimplicial algebras and their chain-level structure, which is relevant to the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: No mathematical error. Note that Hom_{Ab_·} here means strict chain maps, i.e. Z^0 of the Hom complex, not homotopy classes. The F considered are therefore not homotopy invariant; this is implicit and not stated.
The completeness hypotheses on A and B in Prop. 2 are only gestured at (a deleted phrase); on the next page B is assumed stable under projective limits.

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors Ss → A ≅ cosimplicial objects of A ≅ cochain complexes (and dually, limit-preserving Ss^op → B ≅ chain complexes)
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda/Kan extension (density of Δ in sSet) combined with the Dold–Kan correspondence
ideas.where_published: Similar density/extension arguments appear in SGA 4 Exp. I and in Pursuing Stacks; this specific formulation is unsure

ideas.what: Normalized chain complex C_·(X) = N(Z X) as the universal additive invariant; additive limit-preserving invariants are exactly Hom(C_·(X), K) for chain complexes K
ideas.modern_name: Free simplicial abelian group / normalized chains; representability via Dold–Kan

ideas.what: Remark that multiplicative structures on F(X) are not recoverable from C_·(X) alone and require the extra structure C_· carries from X
ideas.modern_name: Coalgebra / E∞-coalgebra structure on chains (Alexander–Whitney, Steenrod cup-i); chain-level Eilenberg–Zilber issues
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod; later May, Mandell (E∞ cochains determine homotopy type, 2001/2006), Berger–Fresse

deep.surprise_reason: This is an expository reformulation of standard Yoneda plus Dold–Kan facts in Grothendieck's 'universal algebra' language. The remark on multiplicative structure requiring extra chain-level structure is well known (E∞/coalgebra structures). Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'additifs[?] F (Ss° → Ab, ...' in conclusion 1° reads 'envisagés F (Ss° → Ab, commutant aux lim)'.
'Ce groupe {+ab.+} semi-simplicial' is written as 'Ce groupe ab/½simplicial', i.e. semi-simplicial with 'ab' inserted above.
The subscript under Hom in a) and b) is 'comm. aux lim' (commutant aux limites); in a) it means inductive limits, in b) projective limits.
In the line '... X_* en faveur de C.(X_*)^* = C. ∈ Ab.', the star is plausibly a superscript annotation; the reading is uncertain.
The boxed formula has subscript F_{K.}, with a corrected subscript visible.
